description:
A school student with a passion for literature and story telling, I am an excellent speaker and communicator.

Looking for students that share the same interests and enjoy learning new things about space.
summary:
We developed a software application through base 44 that enables us to envision the Martian surface as well as the rovers, probes, orbiters, aircraft, and bases that are present on the surface.
The application includes a time-lapse from 1971 to 2021, which enables us to see the arrival of this equipment on the Martian surface.
The application also gives a brief description of all the equipment present on the surface.
Our challenge is to tell a story about abandoned equipment that once had a purpose, and so we chose DS-2, the two-minute probes called 'Scott' and 'Amundsen ', and we best describe their purpose with the help of our application.
It is important because the outcome of the DS-2 was classified as a failure, but their failure led us to prepare better technology to send on the Martian surface.
details:
The project functions to provide brief information about the DS-2 probes in the format of a story. It helps us become aware of the technology that was used to prepare such a minute probe and its intention to understand the Martian surface through signals, and to use the data to identify the faults that occurred during its manufacturing that can be avoided in the creation of the next technology for the same purpose.

Its impact can be measured by the advancement in technology with the creation of the Heat Flow and Physical Properties Package (HP3), which was sent through the InSight lander in 2018.

The tool that was used to create the application was base 44.

The project was creative in such a way that normally we look into equipment that was successfully deployed and functioned properly, but we do often overlook those failed missions that had a purpose, and it is in great need to understand why a mission was unsuccessful, because achievement is reached through failures.
